story.title: Meta takes down a critical video about meta AI Glasses after filming at Meta

draft:
When a whistleblower’s lens gets blurred, the story tells more than the video.

Meta pulled a critical video that exposed flaws in its AI‑powered glasses, citing policy violations. The removal happened just days after the footage was shot on Meta’s own campus, raising questions about how open the company really is to internal dissent.

I see two risks here: first, the loss of a candid feedback loop that could surface design blind spots before they reach users; second, a precedent that any negative narrative about a product can be silenced, eroding trust among engineers and the broader community.

If we want AI wearables to be safe and useful, we need mechanisms that protect honest critique, not just brand reputation. Transparency isn’t a PR stunt—it’s a safety net for emerging tech.

What safeguards would you put in place to ensure critical internal voices are heard without compromising a company’s rollout schedule?

#AI #AR #Meta #TechTransparency #ProductEthics
